pages.text: Every paddy had one place where water trickled down. Trickle, trickle, trickle.
Dingding held a rice bowl in both hands. "I will go to Mr. Ming's alone."
Mom passed with a bucket. "Ten steps along here. Quick, there and back." Grandma watched from above.
Dingding counted. One, two, three... ten.
Ten steps, still high up. No Mr. Ming's place.
More steps. Still nothing. "Grandma, still far!"
The bank path wound this way and that. Mom had said it without counting.
Dingding decided to count falling-water sounds, passing them one by one.
One, two, three. Past the third, Mr. Ming's place!
He took the bowl. Ducks had followed in a line. "Rice smells bring you here without counting!"
